item.title: Teen shot dead after stabbing stranger 'very much enjoyed' extremist content

item.title: Russia, Saudi Arabia and Australia named as biggest CO2 exporters in history
item.description: Analysis of fossil fuel exports since 1850 differs from most assessments – which look at countries where CO 2 is released Russia, Saudi Arabia and Australia are the three biggest exporters of carbon dioxide in history, according to analysis of fossil fuels since 1850. Russia tops the list of global exporters of fossil fuels, with its vast coal, oil and gas deposits. Accounting for the CO 2 produced by burning these exports, Russia has been responsible for more than 70 gigatonnes, up to the end of 2025. Continue reading... Fuente: The Guardian - Environment.

item.description: Funny looks aren't the worst of it, it's the disgusted faces that really get to me. But I don't speak out about this for myself alone. Fuente: ABC News Australia.

item.title: Rio Tinto agrees to pay US$250m to begin repairing ‘devastation’ left by Panguna mine
item.description: Community leader says fund gives chance to find solutions to ‘huge problems we have been living with since the days of the mine’s operation’ Anglo-Australian miner Rio Tinto has agreed to pay a quarter-of-a-billion dollars to begin the clean-up of the toxic Panguna mine site it abandoned more than three decades ago. Panguna, once one of the world’s most profitable gold and copper mines, was shuttered in 1989 after violent protests over environmental damage and the inequitable division of the mine’s profits sparked a decade-long civil war on the Papua New Guinean island of Bougainville… Fuente: The Guardian - World.

item.title: Japanese plan to bury carbon dioxide off Australia raises feasibility doubts
item.description: A Japanese-led plan to bury carbon dioxide (CO2) beneath the seabed off northern Australia is moving closer to reality even as questions have been raised about the project’s commercial viability and its eventual contribution towards Japan’s climate goals. Inpex, the Japanese energy company leading the Bonaparte carbon capture and storage (CCS) project, announced in October that it had begun an initial engineering design, with the first CO2 injections targeted for the early 2030s, pending... Fuente: South China Morning Post.

item.title: Truck driver fired for ‘unsafe’ use of smartglasses in first reported sacking over device in Australia
item.description: Toll employee Ricardo Martins Silva used smartglasses to take photos at an LPG terminal despite the risk of an explosion caused by an electrical spark, a court heard Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast A Toll truck driver was fired from work in Victoria after using smartglasses to snap photos at an LPG terminal, in what was described as an “intrinsically unsafe” incident. It is the first reported case in Australia of a worker dismissed for using smartglasses in a workplace. Continue reading... Fuente: The Guardian - World.
